newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MOORE'S ARRIVAL COULD HASTEN ROY'S DEPARTURE FROM FOREST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MOORE'S ARRIVAL COULD HASTEN ROY'S DEPARTURE FROM FOREST.

text.p: Dutchman Bryan Roy looks set to be shown the door at Nottingham Forest this summer following a public clash with Dave Bassett and Wednesday's arrival of one-million-pound striker Ian Moore from Tranmere.

Forest's new general manager Bassett was considering whether to fine the Dutch international for his show of dissent during the 1-1 draw at Blackburn Rovers on Tuesday, at the same time as tying up the loose ends on 20-year-old Moore's transfer from Tranmere.
Bassett was furious at the way Roy disputed the decision to substitute him at Ewood Park and the gesture of disgust the player made towards first team coach Liam O'Kane.

Bassett said: "I'm not prepared to tolerate that kind of behaviour from anyone and he's looking at a possible fine. What he did is being derogatory to his team mates and to the coaching staff and to me.

"He seems to think he's bigger than the team. This is a team game and players, especially one of his calibre, should be professional enough to deal with it. If he's substituted then that is it and he should accept it, not make public gestures like that and question people's authority.
"Bryan feels he is being made a scapegoat for the situation we're in. I don't know what has given him that impression."

It is the second time in less than a week that Roy has been involved in public dissent with club officials. Last Wednesday he clashed with player-manager Stuart Pearce in the 3-0 defeat by Sheffield Wednesday.
With the signing of Pierre Van Hooydonk and the arrival of England under-21 striker Moore, Roy's days at the City Ground seem to be numbered.
His contract runs out next season and Forest could be ready to allow him to return to the Netherlands for a cut-price fee.
